summary: Healthy Monitor is a full-stack web application designed to track, evaluate, and manage astronauts' vital signs during space missions. Built with an interactive HTML/Bootstrap/JavaScript frontend, a Java backend, and an SQL database, the platform allows crew members and mission administrators to log key physiological indicators—including heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep hours, and oxygen saturation.   The system addresses the challenge of remote space health monitoring by automatically categorizing vital readings into three risk levels (Optimal, Caution, and Critical) and providing immediate, actionable space-medical protocols alongside historical trend charts and educational guides.   In extreme microgravity environments where immediate Earth-based medical intervention is impossible, early detection of physiological anomalies and clear response guidelines are vital to prevent medical emergencies, protect crew performance, and ensure mission success.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Healthy Monitor is a full-stack web application that tracks astronauts' vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, and oxygen). Users log data, and the system automatically evaluates it against orbital thresholds, sorting readings into three risk levels (Optimal, Caution, and Critical). Clicking any card opens step-by-step space-medical protocols.

Benefits and Impact

Fast Decisions: Translates complex clinical data into clear actions during high-stress missions.

Proactive Care: Detects microgravity-related anomalies early to prevent health emergencies.

Tools Used

Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap, and JavaScript.

Backend & Database: Java (Eclipse) and SQL.

Version Control: GitHub.

Creativity and Factors Considered

The design blends a space-themed UI with clean modal guides to prevent cognitive overload. We focused on deep-space autonomy, ensuring crew members can manage health risks independently when communication with Earth is delayed.
